audit.whatIsWrong: The page calls his R a 'lock' in four places (whys[4], spikes[1], mid, wants.foe[2]) and names it 'Final Retribution'. It also describes his W as giving 'resets'.
audit.why: Riot's text for his R: 'rises then stabs downward, damaging enemies and healing for a portion of the damage dealt' — it carries a heal flag and NO CC flag of any kind. There is no lock. The hard displacement in his kit is the Q recast knockup and the W stab, which PULLS enemies toward him from 850 units; W has no reset mechanic at all. Telling a Yi to hold his one escape for a non-existent ultimate lock, while the real threat is a pull into a knockup, gets him killed by the abilities he wasn't watching. The R's real name per the interaction data is Grim Deliverance, and Q is The Darkin Glaive.
audit.corrected: R re-keyed as a self-heal ultimate on 110s with Grievous Wounds as the answer; W described as an 850-range pull; the knockup attributed to the Q recast.
sources: missingInteractions headlines naming The Darkin Glaive (Q) and Grim Deliverance (R)

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere mentions that his passive lets him REVIVE.
audit.why: Zaahen's passive stacks Determination from attacks and abilities against champions, and when filled he gains bonus AD and can revive. For a champion whose whole plan is 'kill him in the sidelane and take the tower', a revive is the single most decision-changing fact on the page, and it was absent.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal, and no mention that his Q is an auto-attack reset.
audit.why: Both his Q and his R heal him, and the page repeatedly frames the lane as racing his drain — unshredded, that race is not winnable. His burst also opens with the Q reset, so the wind-up is the tell rather than the cast.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds written into spikes[1]; the reset tell into early.

Then comes his prime: at 2 E Golden Onslaught reaches you at will and beats your single Alpha Strike answer, and from 3 his full Q-W-E rotation bursts you while W Ominous Return resets deny your trade-backs - give ground, farm with Q, and Meditate the chip away.
edits.after: Level 1 is quiet farming - neither kit has its all-in tools yet. Then comes his prime: at 2 his dash reaches you at will and beats your single Alpha Strike answer, and from 3 the full rotation bursts you - his W stabs from 850 units and pulls you in, and his Q is an auto-reset that heals him. Give ground, farm with Q, and Meditate the chip away.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay his as glaive poke taxes your farm and his stats win every straight commit - survive on CS discipline and jungle presence, not heroics. At 6 the fight finally evens: his R Final Retribution lock is death if it catches you, but Alpha Strike's untargetability dodges the lock window and Highlander's resets flip any fight that goes long.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay his as glaive poke taxes your farm and his stats win every straight commit - survive on CS discipline and jungle presence, not heroics. At 6 the fight finally evens: Grim Deliverance (R) heals him off its own damage on a 110s cooldown, so shred that heal, use Alpha Strike's untargetable window on the stab, and let Highlander's resets flip the long fight.
